description: The exact location and standard time of any place on Earth are determined using latitudes and longitudes. These imaginary lines form a global grid system, which serves as the fundamental basis for geography, cartography, and navigation.

sections.title: Lines of Latitude
sections.description: The angular distance of a place measured from the center of the Earth, North or South of the Equator.

key_concepts.explanation: These are horizontal imaginary lines drawn parallel to the Equator from East to West. They measure distance north or south of the equator.

geographical_data.key_characteristics: It divides the Earth into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres. It is the only latitude that is a Great Circle.
It represents the northernmost limit where the Sun can be seen directly overhead at noon at least once a year (Summer Solstice).
It represents the southernmost limit where the Sun shines directly overhead at noon at least once a year (Winter Solstice).

important_facts.fact: The distance between two parallel lines of latitude is approximately 111 kilometers (69 miles) anywhere on Earth.
The total number of lines of latitude is 179 (excluding the poles as they are points), while the total number of latitudes is 181 (90°N + 90°S + 0° Equator).

sections.title: Lines of Longitude
sections.description: The angular distance of a place measured East or West from the Prime Meridian.

key_concepts.explanation: These are vertical imaginary lines connecting the North Pole to the South Pole. They intersect the equator at right angles and are used to determine local time.

geographical_data.key_characteristics: It divides the Earth into the Eastern and Western Hemispheres and serves as the universal baseline for measuring global time (GMT).

important_facts.fact: Lines of longitude are not parallel; the distance between them is maximum at the Equator (111.3 km) and gradually decreases to zero at the poles.
The total number of longitudes is 360 (180° East + 180° West).

sections.title: Time Zones and Calculation of Time
sections.description: Based on the Earth's rotation, the world is divided into various Time Zones to standardize global timekeeping.

key_concepts.explanation: The time reckoned by the apparent position of the sun in the sky. When the sun reaches its highest point at a specific longitude, it is 12:00 Noon local time.
The uniform time adopted by a country or region, usually based on the local time of a central meridian passing through it, to avoid confusion in transportation and communication.

scientific_principles.application: The Earth completes a 360° rotation in 24 hours (15° per hour). Moving East of the Prime Meridian adds time (+4 mins/degree), while moving West subtracts time (-4 mins/degree).

sections.title: International Date Line (IDL)
sections.description: The globally accepted boundary from where the calendar date officially changes.

key_concepts.explanation: An imaginary zig-zag line approximately following the 180° longitude, passing through the mid-Pacific Ocean, which separates two consecutive calendar days.

scientific_principles.principle_or_law: Rule of Date Change across IDL
scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: Crossing West to East = Subtract 1 Day (-1) | Crossing East to West = Add 1 Day (+1)
scientific_principles.application: When a traveler crosses the IDL from the Eastern Hemisphere to the Western Hemisphere (Asia to America), they repeat a day. When crossing from West to East (America to Asia), they skip a day.

important_facts.fact: The International Date Line is not a straight line; it deviates at several places (like the Bering Strait, Fiji, and Tonga) to prevent a single country or island group from operating on two different dates.

sections.title: In the Context of India
sections.description: The application of geographical coordinates to determine India's standard time and climatic zones.

geographical_data.key_characteristics: It passes through Mirzapur in Uttar Pradesh and is exactly 5 hours and 30 minutes ahead of Greenwich Mean Time (GMT +5:30).
It divides India into almost two equal halves and passes through 8 states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, and Mizoram.

important_facts.fact: India's longitudinal extent is about 30 degrees, which creates a time difference of nearly 2 hours between its westernmost point in Gujarat and easternmost point in Arunachal Pradesh.
The Mahi River in western India is the only river in the country that cuts across the Tropic of Cancer twice.
